resolved_findings.detail: The new set comparison is case-sensitive, while the fixed SQLite SELECTs are case-insensitive. An ordinary exporter-produced APKG with only col/notes/cards renamed to COL/NOTES/CARDS imports one row with the HEAD baseline, but the new importer rejects all three as missing ordinary tables. This changes acceptance of valid ordinary source tables beyond the intended view/virtual exclusion.
resolved_findings.resolution: APKG normalizes ordinary table names with name.lower() before required-name comparison; shared metadata helper retains native type filtering. Six upper/title-case tests for all three names pass.
resolved_findings.suggested_change: Normalize the required-name comparison consistently with SQLite ASCII case-insensitive identifiers, and add an ordinary mixed-case APKG regression. Preserve exact native type filtering.
resolved_findings.title: Preserve SQLite case-insensitive table-name compatibility

tests.final_schema_security_run: 19 passed in 0.14s, including six new case-insensitive compatibility cases

verified_behavior: PRAGMA main.table_list native type==table excludes views, virtual tables, and shadow tables; STRICT and WITHOUT ROWID ordinary tables remain accepted.
Both supported SQLite row representations (tuples and sqlite3.Row) work with index-based helper access.
Empty unsupported PRAGMA metadata fails closed with the documented minimum-version message; APKG converts ValueError to APKGImportError.
sqlite3.Error during metadata or later SELECT remains translated by the existing outer handler. The endpoint maps APKGImportError to HTTP 400.
All three source table names are checked together before any imported-content SELECT; media asset importer calls occur later.
OpenWebUI preserves its prior native metadata/type checks; the shared helper changes only error prefix and tuple-index access.
No temporary-schema shadow path exists from uploaded APKG bytes because importer creates a fresh connection. Metadata preparation/parser behavior is explicitly outside the claimed fix.

limits: No malformed/corrupted exploit databases, ML imports or model execution.
Metadata inspection itself can prepare schemas; not complete SQLite parser remediation.
Admin-only raw database restore remains a separate intentional authority boundary.
Retained images predate both import fixes and do not receive a SQLite exception from new source changes.

reviewed_callers.match_path: No first-party MATCH on the uploaded connection after the guard; virtual-table/view substitution for required names is rejected. Existing TASK31 metadata-preparation limitation is retained; this is not proof against every malformed SQLite parser input.
reviewed_callers.source_pages: Externally supplied SQLite pages are opened read-only. Required source names user/folder/chat/file/chat_file must have parsed table_list type=table before SELECT.

reviewed_callers.entry: Authenticated POST /api/v1/flashcards/import/apkg with default import limits; admin required only for limit overrides.
reviewed_callers.match_path: Static inference from SQLite documented view semantics: these required names can be views whose SELECT evaluates uploaded FTS5 MATCH. No crafted database, SQLite fixture, or memory-corruption exploit was created or executed in this review.
reviewed_callers.needed_change: Require ordinary source tables before content queries, with boundary regressions. Parent tracks this separately as TASK-13013.7.36. Source acceptance is confirmed; exact retained-library CVE impact remains unresolved.
reviewed_callers.source_pages: ZIP collection.anki2/collection.anki21 bytes are written into a temporary file and opened with sqlite3.connect. col, notes and cards are SELECTed without requiring ordinary tables.

reviewed_callers.authority: An administrator is authorized to replace whole databases. This is a real privileged page-ingress path, not a newly confirmed authorization defect or memory-corruption reproduction. Admin database-restore privilege is not itself proof of arbitrary native-code execution authority.
reviewed_callers.match_path: After successful chacha restore with the compatible application schema, ordinary GET /flashcards?q reaches list_flashcards/count_flashcards and flashcards_fts MATCH on restored pages. Media search independently uses media_fts MATCH. No logical row reconstruction or FTS rebuild is performed in the restore copy.
reviewed_callers.source_pages: Caller uploads bundle manifest plus SQLite files. Size/SHA checks use the same supplied manifest and establish consistency, not trusted origin. Dataset resolution selects live chacha/media paths; restore_sqlite_database_file copies source pages using Connection.backup.

reviewed_callers.entry: Native chatbook ZIP import including conversations, notes, embeddings and stored media
reviewed_callers.match_path: Conflict searches and later searches operate on the server database. Text values may influence queries but do not supply raw FTS page encodings; no package-wide safety conclusion follows.
reviewed_callers.source_pages: Conversation/embedding content is JSON and note content is logical text/metadata; records are inserted through server database methods. Stored artifact bytes go under per-user imported_media/media_ID/UUID_filename and do not replace live database files.

reviewed_callers.match_path: Reviewed attachment-copy path opens files as bytes and processes attachment content; it does not sqlite3.connect attachment bytes. This does not claim document parser safety.
reviewed_callers.source_pages: The separate webui.db connection receives TASK31 import and file/chat_file table guards. Attachment copies use per-user media/media_ID storage, not a database replacement destination.

reviewed_callers.match_path: If backup bytes originated externally, the same later MATCH risk applies; otherwise this is a server-created backup. A local operator replacement of the backup file is a separate write-authority prerequisite.
reviewed_callers.source_pages: Dataset-specific backup directory and validated backup_id select an existing backup file, followed by the same page-copy helper. This API does not itself upload new raw SQLite bytes.
